# Testing a package that simd depends on makes the go command compile a test
# variant of it, and rebuild the importers it knows about against that variant.
# simd is not among them, so a rewritten package linked into the same test binary
# would see two different builds of strconv and fail to link. internal/fuzz has a
# loop the wrapper would rewrite, imports strconv, and every test binary links it
# (through testing/internal/testdeps): it must be left alone here.
#
# The wrapper normally notices that strconv is being tested and rewrites nothing (see
# toolexec_tests_simd_dependency.txt). That check reads the go command's command
# line and does not exist on every platform, so it is turned off here to exercise
# the protection that remains. That protection only covers the packages built
# against a variant: another rewritten package in the test binary still links
# simd, which is why the test may fail to link (on a toolchain where os is not a
# simd dependency, internal/filepathlite is one). The variant it names is the
# first in import path order, fmt where fmt is a simd dependency.

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_NO_TARGET_CHECK=1
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_DEBUG=1
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=internal/fuzz
? exec go test -short -run 'TestAtoi|TestItoa' -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC strconv
grep -count=1 '^skipped internal/fuzz: built against a test variant of (fmt|strconv)$' log
! grep '^rewrote' log

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
